# Sluz

> Sluz is a minimalistic, zero-dependency, single-file PHP templating engine with
> Smarty-like syntax. It separates logic (.php files) from presentation (.stpl
> templates). Requires PHP 8.0 or newer.

This file contains the full text of every Sluz documentation example: the PHP source
and the paired template for each page. The short index is in llms.txt.

## Syntax Reference

This section summarizes the template language as implemented in `sluz.class.php`
(engine version 0.9.8). The examples below show each feature.

### Blocks and delimiters

- Blocks are wrapped in `{` and `}`. Text outside blocks is output unchanged.
- A `{` with whitespace on both sides is plain text. This is why CSS and JavaScript
  braces usually work without `{literal}`.
- Whitespace just inside a block, such as `{$x }` or `{ $x}`, is an error (50981).
  The exception is a `{` with whitespace on both sides, which is plain text.
- Delimiters can be changed with `set_delimiters('[', ']')`. Both must be single,
  different characters. Comments then use `[*` and `*]`.

### Comments

```text
{* This is a comment and produces no output. It may span
   several lines. *}
```

The line ending after a comment is removed from the output.

### Variables

- `{$name}` prints the value. An unassigned variable prints nothing.
- Dot notation reads array keys: `{$user.name.first}`. Numeric keys work too: `{$list.0}`.
- An array printed directly outputs the word `Array`.
- `{$name|default:"Guest"}` uses the fallback when the value is unset, null, or empty.
  The fallback must be a quoted string or a number, not a variable.
- Assign several values at once with `$s->assign(['key' => 'value', ...])`.

### Modifiers

- `{$value|function}` calls the PHP function `function($value)`. The variable is always
  the first argument.
- Chain modifiers with more `|` characters: `{$name|strtolower|ucfirst}`.
- Pass arguments after a colon, separated by commas: `{$name|substr:0,3}`.
  Arguments are quoted strings or numbers. Variables are not supported as arguments.
- Any callable function works, including your own functions defined in PHP.
- Unknown functions produce error 47204. Exceptions and type errors produce 79134 and
  58200.

### Escaping

- `{$value|escape}` encodes HTML. This is the default type.
- `{$value|escape:"url"}` uses `rawurlencode()`.
- `{$value|escape:"js"}` returns a JSON string, including the surrounding double
  quotes. Use it without adding quotes of your own: `var v = {$value|escape:"js"};`.
- An unknown escape type outputs an error string (65491) instead of stopping the script.
- `$s->setEscapeHtml(true)` escapes every `{$var}`. Use `|raw` or `|escape` to opt out
  for one value.

### Expressions

Blocks that are not variables, `if`, `foreach`, `include`, or `literal` are evaluated as
PHP expressions:

```text
{$count + 3}
{3 + 4}
{"Hello" . " " . $name}
```

The result must be a string or a number. Booleans and null produce error 18933. Blocks
that contain no quotes, digits, `$`, or parentheses are rejected as unknown blocks
(73467).

### If, elseif, else

```text
{if $score >= 90}A{elseif $score >= 80}B{else}C{/if}
```

- The syntax is `{elseif condition}`. The space after `elseif` is required.
- Comparisons: `==`, `!=`, `===`, `!==`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`.
- Logic: `!`, `&&`, `||`, and parentheses.
- An unassigned variable is treated as false. `{if !$missing}` is true.
- Word operators such as `eq` and `ne` are not supported.
- A missing `{/if}` produces error 45821.

### Foreach

```text
{foreach $items as $item}{$item}{/foreach}
{foreach $hash as $key => $value}{$key}: {$value}{/foreach}
{foreach $user.tags as $tag}{$tag}{/foreach}
```

- The source can be a dotted path.
- A scalar source loops once. A null source loops zero times.
- `$__FOREACH_FIRST`, `$__FOREACH_LAST`, and `$__FOREACH_INDEX` are set inside the loop.
  They are only computed when the block uses them.
- Loop variables do not exist after the `{/foreach}`.

### Include

```text
{include file='tpls/header.stpl'}
{include file='tpls/card.stpl' title="Welcome" size="large"}
```

- Paths are relative to the directory of the PHP script that calls `fetch()`.
- Extra `key="value"` pairs are assigned to the included template. Values must be quoted.
  Variables may appear inside double quotes, such as `"$name"`.
- Variables set for the include are restored after it finishes.
- A missing file produces error 18485 or 68493.

### Literal

```text
{literal}function f() { return {a: 1}; }{/literal}
```

Content inside `{literal}` is output unchanged, including any `{...}` blocks.

### Parent and child templates

- `$s->fetch('child.stpl', 'parent.stpl')` renders the child inside the parent.
- `$s->parent_tpl('parent.stpl')` sets a parent for every later `fetch()`.
- The parent template receives `$__CHILD_TPL`, the child's path. Include it with
  `{include file="$__CHILD_TPL"}`.

### PHP API

```php
$s = new sluz();
$s->assign('name', 'value');
$s->assign(['k1' => 'v1', 'k2' => 'v2']);
print $s->fetch('tpls/page.stpl');             // Template file
print $s->parse_string('Hello {$name}');       // String template
$s->display('tpls/page.stpl');                 // Same as print fetch()
print $s->fetch(SLUZ_INLINE);                  // Template after __halt_compiler();
$s->setEscapeHtml(true);                       // Auto-escape {$var} output
$s->set_delimiters('[', ']');                  // Change delimiters
```

`sluz()` in simple mode sets a value and returns the object. Its output is printed
automatically when the script ends.

### Error output

Most errors print an HTML page with a code and message, then stop the script.
Code 65491 is the exception described under Escaping.

| Code  | Meaning                                  |
|-------|------------------------------------------|
| 18485 | Unable to load include template          |
| 18933 | Bad function, expression, or condition   |
| 42280 | Unable to load template file             |
| 45821 | Unclosed tag, such as a missing `{/if}`  |
| 47204 | Unknown function call in a modifier      |
| 50981 | Whitespace next to delimiters            |
| 58200 | TypeError in a modifier call             |
| 65491 | Unknown escape type                      |
| 68493 | Missing file in an include block         |
| 73467 | Unknown block type                       |
| 79134 | Exception in a modifier call             |

### Security

Expressions and conditions are run with PHP `eval()`. Only use templates that you
control, and never use user input as template source.

## 001_basic_vars

Source: https://www.sluz.org/docs/?doc=001_basic_vars

### 001_basic_vars.php

```php
<?php

///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
// Basic syntax for assigning variables to the templating system. You can    //
// assign scalars, arrays, and hashes.                                       //
///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

include("../sluz.class.php");
$s = new sluz();

$s->assign("first", "Jason"); // Scalar syntax
$s->assign("last" , "Doolis");

$s->assign("month", ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar"]); // Array syntax
$s->assign("data" , ["color" => "red"]);    // Hash syntax

print $s->fetch("tpls/001_basic_vars.stpl");
```

### 001_basic_vars.stpl

```text
<h1>Welcome</h1>

<p>Hello {$first} {$last}</p>

<p>The first month of the year is {$month.0}</p>

<p>My favorite color is {$data.color}</p>
```

## 002_default_values

Source: https://www.sluz.org/docs/?doc=002_default_values

### 002_default_values.php

```php
<?php

///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
// A variable that is: null, empty string, or not assign() can be given      //
// a default value in the template.                                          //
//                                                                           //
// Note: The default value must be a scalar (not a variable)                 //
///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

include("../sluz.class.php");
$s = new sluz();

$s->assign("name", "Jason Doolis");
//$s->assign("greeting", "Hola"); // If we don't send this, the default it used

print $s->fetch("tpls/002_default_values.stpl");
```

### 002_default_values.stpl

```text
<p>{$greeting|default:"Hello"} {$name}</p>
```

## 010_basic_if

Source: https://www.sluz.org/docs/?doc=010_basic_if

### 010_basic_if.php

```php
<?php

///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
// Conditional syntax is available in the form of if/else.                   //
//                                                                           //
// Note: When an if statement references a variable that is *not assigned it //
// will be treated as if it were false.                                      //
///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

include("../sluz.class.php");
$s = new sluz();

$s->assign("weekday", date("D"));
$s->assign("kitten_count", 7);
$s->assign("verbose", true);

print $s->fetch("tpls/010_basic_if.stpl");
```

### 010_basic_if.stpl

```text
{if $weekday === "Wed"}
<h1>It is Wednesday</h1>
{else}
<h1>It is not Wednesday</h1>
{/if}

{if $kitten_count > 4}<p>You have a lot of kittens</p>{/if}

{if !$quiet}<div>Here is some detailed information</div>{/if}

{if $verbose && !$quiet}Since we are not quiet, here is even more information{/if}
```

## 030_basic_foreach

Source: https://www.sluz.org/docs/?doc=030_basic_foreach

### 030_basic_foreach.php

```php
<?php

///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
// Foreach works just like native PHP, on either arrays or hashes.           //
//                                                                           //
// Array syntax: {foreach $foo as $bar}                                      //
// Hash syntax : {foreach $foo as $key => $val}                              //
///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

include("../sluz.class.php");
$s = new sluz();

$s->assign("turtles", ["Michelangeo", "Donatello", "Leonardo", "Raphael"]); // Array
$s->assign("numbers", ["one" => "uno", "two" => "dos", "three" => "tres"]); // Hash

print $s->fetch("tpls/030_basic_foreach.stpl");
```

### 030_basic_foreach.stpl

```text
<ul>
{foreach $turtles as $name}
	<li>{$name}</li>
{/foreach}
</ul>

{foreach $numbers as $english => $spanish}
<div>{$english} => {$spanish}</div>
{/foreach}
```

## 031_advanced_foreach

Source: https://www.sluz.org/docs/?doc=031_advanced_foreach

### 031_advanced_foreach.php

```php
<?php

///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
// {foreach} blocks apply special variables on each loop interation. They    //
// are: $__FOREACH_FIRST, $__FOREACH_LAST, $__FOREACH_INDEX. First/Last will //
// be true if it is either first of last interation, and the index will be   //
// set the loop iteration number (starting at zero).                         //
///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

include("../sluz.class.php");
$s = new sluz();

$s->assign("turtles", ["Michelangelo", "Donatello", "Leonardo", "Raphael"]); // Array

print $s->fetch("tpls/031_advanced_foreach.stpl");
```

### 031_advanced_foreach.stpl

```text
<p>
{foreach $turtles as $name}
<div style="background: {if $__FOREACH_FIRST}orange{elseif $__FOREACH_LAST}red{else}yellow{/if}">{$name}</div>
{/foreach}
</p>

<p>
{foreach $turtles as $name}
<div>{$__FOREACH_INDEX}) {$name}</div>
{/foreach}
</p>
```

## 040_literal_blocks

Source: https://www.sluz.org/docs/?doc=040_literal_blocks

### 040_literal_blocks.php

```php
<?php

///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
// You may need a literal '{' or '}' in your HTML. These characters are      //
// common in both CSS and Javascript. To prevent Sluz from interpretting     //
// them as code blocks use {literal}.                                        //
//                                                                           //
// Note: Brackets with whitespace on both sides do NOT require {literal}     //
///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

include("../sluz.class.php");
$s = new sluz();

$s->assign("name", "Jason Doolis");

print $s->fetch("tpls/040_literal_blocks.stpl");
```

### 040_literal_blocks.stpl

```text
<script>
	var name = "{$name}";

	{literal}
	function hello_world() {
		alert("Hi there " + name);
	}
	{/literal}
</script>

<button onclick="hello_world();">Click me</button>
```

## 045_include

Source: https://www.sluz.org/docs/?doc=045_include

### 045_include.php

```php
<?php

///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
// You can include external templates in your .stpl files. This allows you   //
// to have a common header, footer, or framework. Included files have all    //
// the same properties as normal templates. Templates in {include} tags      //
// need to be pathed *relative* to the calling PHP script.                   //
///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

include("../sluz.class.php");
$s = new sluz();

$s->assign("first", "Jason"); // Scalar syntax
$s->assign("last" , "Doolis");

print $s->fetch("tpls/045_include.stpl");
```

### 045_include.stpl

```text
{include file='tpls/header.stpl'}

<p>Hello {$first} {$last}</p>
```

## 046_external_functions

Source: https://www.sluz.org/docs/?doc=046_external_functions

### 046_external_functions.php

```php
<?php

///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
// Templates can call external functions. Any function that is callable in   //
// normal scope can be used: global PHP functions, or user functions.        //
// Functions will be called with the template variable being the first       //
// parameter, and other params after.                                        //
//                                                                           //
// Example: `{$name|strtoupper}` maps to `strtoupper($name)`                 //
// Example: `{$name|substr:0,3}` maps to `substr($name, 0, 3)`               //
///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

include("../sluz.class.php");
$s = new sluz();

$s->assign("name" , "Jason Doolis"); // Scalar syntax
$s->assign("numbers" , [4,1,9,7,2]); // Array syntax

print $s->fetch("tpls/046_external_functions.stpl");

///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

function join_comma(array $arr, string $separator = ", ") {
	return join($separator, $arr);
}

function initials($str) {
	$ret = '';

	foreach (preg_split('/ /', $str) as $x) { $ret .= substr($x, 0, 1); }

	return $ret;
}
```

### 046_external_functions.stpl

```text
<p>Uppercase: {$name|strtoupper}</p>
<p>Initials: {$name|initials}</p>
<p>Numbers Comma: {$numbers|join_comma}</p>
<p>Numbers Semi-colon: {$numbers|join_comma:"; "}</p>
<p>Substring: {$name|substr:0,3}</p>
```

## 047_alternate_templates

Source: https://www.sluz.org/docs/?doc=047_alternate_templates

### 047_alternate_templates.php

```php
<?php

///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
// If you want to use an alternate template specify it when you call fetch() //
///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

include("../sluz.class.php");
$s = new sluz();

$s->assign("name", "Jason Doolis"); // Scalar syntax
$hour = date("H");

if ($hour > 17) {
	print $s->fetch("tpls/dark_mode.stpl");
} else {
	print $s->fetch("tpls/light_mode.stpl");
}
```

### 047_alternate_templates.stpl

```text
<body style="background: lightgray; color: black">Light mode</body>
```

## 050_simple_mode

Source: https://www.sluz.org/docs/?doc=050_simple_mode

### 050_simple_mode.php

```php
<?php

///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
// Simple mode allows you to use a function oriented syntax instead of the   //
// object oriented syntax. This decreases the number of function calls       //
// needed to run sluz. Less typing = better?                                 //
///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

require('../sluz.class.php');

// sluz() is an alias for $s->assign($key, $value) and returns a sluz object
$s = sluz("weather", "Sure is sunny today");
$s = sluz("temperature", 75);

// Note: fetch() is called automatically in simple mode as part of the destructor.
// The template file used is the PHP filename with the `.php` changed to `.stpl`
// in the `tpls/` directory. Example: `myscript.php` => `/tpls/myscript.stpl`
//
// If you need an alternate template you will need to call fetch() manually:
// print $s->fetch("tpls/special.stpl");
```

### 050_simple_mode.stpl

```text
<h1>Welcome to the weather page</h1>

<h3>{$weather}</h3>

<p>It is {$temperature} degrees outside</p>
```

## 060_inline_mode

Source: https://www.sluz.org/docs/?doc=060_inline_mode

### 060_inline_mode.php

```php
<?php

///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
// Instead of loading a template file we can use a template that is inline   //
// with your PHP code. We use the __halt_compiler() pragma to allow us to    //
// insert template content into PHP files.                                   //
///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

require('../sluz.class.php');

$s = new sluz;
$s->assign("name", "Jason Doolis");
$s->assign("turtles", ["Michelangeo", "Donatello", "Leonardo", "Raphael"]);

print $s->fetch(SLUZ_INLINE);

////////////////////////////////////////////////////

__halt_compiler();

<h1>Hello {$name}</h1>

{foreach $turtles as $t}
<div>{$t}</div>
{/foreach}
```

## 065_inline_simple_mode

Source: https://www.sluz.org/docs/?doc=065_inline_simple_mode

### 065_inline_simple_mode.php

```php
<?php

///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
// Combine both inline mode, and simple mode to minimize the lines of code   //
// required to instatiate and call Sluz. This also combines your logic and   //
// presentation in to one file. Great for simple projects.                   //
///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

require('../sluz.class.php');

// Use hash mode to send multiple items at once
$data = ['name' => 'Jason', 'age' => 13, 'animal' => 'kitten'];
$s    = sluz($data);

////////////////////////////////////////////////////

__halt_compiler();

<h1>Hello {$name}</h1>

<p>I am {$age} years old and I really like my {$animal}</p>
```

## 070_parent_child

Source: https://www.sluz.org/docs/?doc=070_parent_child

### 070_parent_child.php

```php
<?php

////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
// It's common to have a global header/footer and include content in the  //
// middle. This can be accomplished with a parent template. When a parent //
// template is specified $__CHILD_TPL is populated with the original      //
// template filename. This can then be {include file="$__CHILD_TPL"} in   //
// the parent.                                                            //
////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

require('../sluz.class.php');
$s = new sluz();

// Two parameter fetch()
print $s->fetch("tpls/070_child.stpl", "tpls/070_parent.stpl");

// You can also set a parent template and then use normal fetch()
//$s->parent_tpl("tpls/070_parent.stpl");
//print $s->fetch("tpls/070_child.stpl");
```

### 070_parent.stpl

```text
<h2>Header</h2>
{include file="$__CHILD_TPL"}
<h4>Footer</h4>
```

### 070_child.stpl

```text
This content is from <code>070_child.stpl</code>
```

## 080_escape

Source: https://www.sluz.org/docs/?doc=080_escape

### 080_escape.php

```php
<?php

///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
// The escape modifier safely encodes output to prevent XSS.                 //
// Supported types: 'html' (default), 'url', and 'js'.                       //
///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

include("../sluz.class.php");
$s = new sluz();

$s->assign("name", "<script>alert('XSS')</script>");
$s->assign("url_path", "hello world");
$s->assign("js_val", "It's a \"test\"");

print $s->fetch("tpls/080_escape.stpl");
```

### 080_escape.stpl

```text
<h1>Escape Modifier</h1>

<p>HTML escaped: {$name|escape}</p>

<p>URL escaped: {$url_path|escape:"url"}</p>

<p>JS escaped: {$js_val|escape:"js"}</p>
```

## 085_autoescape

Source: https://www.sluz.org/docs/?doc=085_autoescape

### 085_autoescape.php

```php
<?php

///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
// Auto-escape mode automatically HTML-encodes all {$var} output.            //
// Use |raw to opt out for trusted content.                                  //
///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

include("../sluz.class.php");
$s = new sluz();

$s->setEscapeHtml(true);

$s->assign("name"        , "<b>Scott</b>");
$s->assign("user_input"  , "<script>alert('XSS')</script>");
$s->assign("trusted_html", "<em>Safe HTML</em>");

print $s->fetch("tpls/085_autoescape.stpl");
```

### 085_autoescape.stpl

```text
<h1>Auto-escape Mode</h1>

<p>Raw variable: {$name}</p>

<p>User input (auto-escaped): {$user_input}</p>

<p>Trusted HTML with |raw: {$trusted_html|raw}</p>

<p>Chained with |escape (no double-escape): {$user_input|escape}</p>

<p>Chained with |strtoupper then auto-escaped: {$name|strtoupper}</p>
```
